newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila orders forex cover of oil firms phased out.
newsitem.headline: Manila orders forex cover of oil firms phased out.

text.p: The Philippine Department of Finance said on Monday it had issued an order to gradually phase out the 90-day foreign exchange cover of oil companies beginning January 1, 1997.

The cover will be cut by 30 days each in the following months, and will be completely abolished by March 1, 1997 in preparation for full deregulation of the local oil industry, it said in a statement.

"Given the very stable exchange rate between the peso and the dollar, and the country's healthy international reserves, the Department of Finance expects little or no impact on the foreign exchange rate," the statement said.

The government estimated that oil companies will pay $540 million in March 1997 as a result of the phaseout. It said the average monthly requirement of dollars for oil crude oil imports is $180 million.
The government, however, said it expected oil companies to obtain financing to soften the impact of the removal of the forward cover.

The original schedule for cutting back on the forward cover was to begin on December 1, 1996 but it was deferred because of a request by Manila's three oil firms, Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp, a unit of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group Caltex (Philippines) Inc and Petron Corp.
The firms had sought the deferment on grounds the government still owed them money from an oil buffer fund.
The forward foreign exchange cover meant that the government took the risk of fluctuations in the peso-dollar exchange rate on behalf of the oil importers.
